findings.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:164 — [P1; confidence: 100] The `Prisma.sql` predicate `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)` has no integration test that executes its array-bound org/team authorization branch through `$queryRaw`, so a PostgreSQL parameter-shape regression exposes or hides org/team bookings without being caught by this raw-query conversion's verification.

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:295 — [100/P2 advisory] The team- and org-scope tests construct an expected `Prisma.sql\`((\"teamId\" = ${testData.team.id}) AND (\"isTeamBooking\" = true)) OR ...\`` fragment and only compare objects, so malformed raw SQL or parameter encoding in those branches passes the suite instead of failing at the `$queryRaw` execution boundary; the user-scope execution test at lines 480-491 does not exercise either branch.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:164 — [P1; confidence: 100] The `Prisma.sql` predicate `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)` has no integration test that executes its array-bound org/team authorization branch through `$queryRaw`, so a PostgreSQL parameter-shape regression exposes or hides org/team bookings without being caught by this raw-query conversion's verification.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's no integration test for the org authorization branch with array-bound teamIds. However, looking at the diff, the test 'should return org conditions for org owner' (lines 329-345 in the test file) explicitly tests the org scope with multiple teams (testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id) and verifies the SQL condition includes `("teamId" = ANY(${[...]})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`. Additionally, the 'getBaseConditions' test at line 477+ executes actual $queryRaw with the base conditions. The finding incorrectly states there's no test coverage for this branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:295 — [100/P2 advisory] The team- and org-scope tests construct an expected `Prisma.sql\`((\"teamId\" = ${testData.team.id}) AND (\"isTeamBooking\" = true)) OR ...\`` fragment and only compare objects, so malformed raw SQL or parameter encoding in those branches passes the suite instead of failing at the `$queryRaw` execution boundary; the user-scope execution test at lines 480-491 does not exercise either branch.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the team-scope and org-scope tests (lines 292-345) only compare the returned Prisma.sql objects using expect().toEqual() without actually executing them against the database. The only test that executes raw SQL via $queryRaw is the 'getBaseConditions' test at lines 477-491, which uses user-scope (scope: 'user'). This means malformed SQL in the org-scope or team-scope branches (buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, buildTeamAuthorizationCondition) would not be caught by actual database execution. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added raw SQL generation logic.
